plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A journeyman is bidding a four-story apartment in a city that adopted the International Plumbing Code. Unless the ordinance amends it, which model code governs the plumbing?

options.a: The ICC International Plumbing Code as adopted by the city
options.b: The IAPMO Uniform Plumbing Code even though the city listed IPC
options.c: NFPA 54 fuel-gas rules used as the whole plumbing code
options.d: ASME A112 fixture standards standing in for the plumbing code

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Jurisdictions adopt a model plumbing code by ordinance. Where the city adopted the IPC, that ICC document—plus any local amendments—is the enforceable plumbing code. The UPC is a different IAPMO model code and is not in force unless the city adopted it instead.

distractorExplanations.b: IAPMO's Uniform Plumbing Code is a separate model; it does not override a city's IPC adoption.
distractorExplanations.c: NFPA 54 covers fuel gas, not the full plumbing system of fixtures, DWV, and water supply.
distractorExplanations.d: ASME A112 standards list fixtures and fittings; they are not a substitute for the adopted plumbing code.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: Permit drawings for a medical office cite the Uniform Plumbing Code throughout the spec. Which organization publishes that model code?

options.a: ICC, the publisher of the International Plumbing Code (IPC)
options.b: NFPA, the publisher of NFPA 54 fuel gas and fire codes
options.c: IAPMO, which writes and publishes the Uniform Plumbing Code
options.d: ASME, through A112 fixture and fitting product standards series

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: The Uniform Plumbing Code is IAPMO's model plumbing code. ICC publishes the IPC, NFPA publishes fire and fuel-gas documents, and ASME writes product standards such as A112—none of those bodies publish the UPC.

distractorExplanations.a: ICC publishes the IPC, a competing model code, not the Uniform Plumbing Code.
distractorExplanations.b: NFPA publishes NFPA 54, NFPA 13, and related fire/fuel-gas codes, not the UPC.
distractorExplanations.d: ASME A112 addresses fixtures and fittings; ASME does not publish the UPC model code.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A listed vacuum breaker is on the truck, but the inspector says it cannot be used on this hose bibb. Who has final approval authority in that jurisdiction?

options.a: The model-code publisher that wrote the adopted code text
options.b: The general contractor managing the overall construction project
options.c: The listing laboratory that certified the plumbing product
options.d: The local official or office that enforces the adopted code

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: The Authority Having Jurisdiction is the local official or office that adopts, interprets, and enforces the plumbing code and issues permits. Listing and model-code text inform that decision, but they do not replace the AHJ's approval power.

distractorExplanations.a: ICC and IAPMO write model codes but have no local enforcement or permit power.
distractorExplanations.b: The contractor must comply; the contractor is not the enforcing authority.
distractorExplanations.c: Listing labs certify products to a standard; the AHJ still decides job-site approval.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A homeowner asks the journeyman to skip the permit on a water-heater change-out to finish before a weekend. Why must the permit still be obtained?

options.a: So the AHJ can inspect the work for public health and safety
options.b: So the city assumes all liability if the work later fails
options.c: So the manufacturer warranty on the heater can be registered
options.d: So the assessor can revalue the house for property taxes

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Plumbing permits exist so the AHJ can review and inspect work that affects public health and safety—gas, combustion air, T&P relief, and potable connections. Skipping the permit hides those checks; it does not transfer liability or create a warranty.

distractorExplanations.b: A permit does not shift defect liability onto the city; it triggers code inspections.
distractorExplanations.c: Warranties are registered with the manufacturer, not created by the plumbing permit.
distractorExplanations.d: Assessors may see permit data, but the code purpose is health-and-safety inspection.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: The water utility requires a reduced-pressure backflow assembly on a fire-sprinkler tap from the domestic main. What is the cross-connection program meant to prevent?

options.a: Sewer gas entering occupied rooms through dry fixture traps
options.b: Keep contaminated water from entering the potable supply
options.c: Keep storm inflow from entering the building sanitary sewer
options.d: Water-hammer surges on the municipal distribution main

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Cross-connection control stops backflow of nonpotable or contaminated water into the potable system. Fire lines, irrigation, and boilers are typical hazards; approved backflow assemblies and testing programs protect the public water supply.

distractorExplanations.a: Sewer gas is controlled by traps and vents, not by backflow assemblies on the water main.
distractorExplanations.c: Storm inflow is an I&I or storm-drain issue, not a potable-water cross-connection program.
distractorExplanations.d: Surge control is hydraulic; cross-connection programs address contamination, not hammer.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A supplier offers unmarked pipe that 'the last crew ran for years' on a potable riser. When is a material approved under the plumbing code?

options.a: When the manufacturer labels the box as plumbing-grade stock
options.b: When the contractor has used the same unmarked product on prior jobs
options.c: When it is listed for that use to a code-referenced standard
options.d: When one listing for DWV automatically covers potable pressure

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Code-approved materials are those listed or accepted for the intended use to a referenced standard and accepted by the AHJ. A maker's marketing label or prior-job habit is not approval, and a DWV listing does not authorize potable pressure service.

distractorExplanations.a: A manufacturer's own 'plumbing-grade' sticker is not a listing to a referenced standard.
distractorExplanations.b: Field familiarity is not code approval; unmarked pipe cannot be accepted on that basis.
distractorExplanations.d: Listings are use-specific; DWV-rated pipe is not automatically approved for potable pressure.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A single bathroom group—water closet, lavatory, and tub—needs a new vent. Unless the local table is stricter, what size does the vent typically start at?

options.a: 1/2 inch, matching a typical lavatory or ice-maker supply
options.b: 3/4 inch, matching a common water-heater T&P relief line
options.c: 1 inch nominal, matching many fixture cold-supply risers
options.d: 1-1/2 inches, the usual start for a bathroom-group vent

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Model codes set a minimum vent of 1-1/4 inch, and a bathroom group that includes a water closet is commonly vented at 1-1/2 inch (or larger per the local DFU table). Half-inch through 1-inch sizes are supply tubing, not DWV vents.

distractorExplanations.a: 1/2 inch is a water-supply size; it is far below the code minimum vent diameter.
distractorExplanations.b: 3/4 inch is a relief or supply size and is below the 1-1/4 inch vent minimum.
distractorExplanations.c: 1 inch still undersizes the vent; bathroom-group vents typically start at 1-1/2 inch.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: Remote lavatories starve when several fixtures run at once, even though the meter looks large. How does the plumbing code size water piping?

options.a: Fixture units, developed length, and remaining pressure
options.b: Drainage fixture units plus the slope of the building drain
options.c: A velocity cap only, ignoring friction over developed length
options.d: Meter size alone, matched to the building main shutoff valve

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Water-supply sizing uses water-supply fixture units, developed length, and available pressure (minus friction and elevation). Velocity limits are a check, not the whole method. Drainage fixture units and slope size the DWV system, not the supply.

distractorExplanations.b: DFUs and slope size drains and vents; they do not size potable supply piping.
distractorExplanations.c: Velocity matters, but friction over developed length and remaining pressure also control size.
distractorExplanations.d: The meter is one constraint; branches are still sized from fixture units, length, and pressure.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A client wants shower and laundry waste stored and pumped to landscape irrigation. Where gray water is allowed, what must the system do?

options.a: Tie into the potable supply through a single check valve
options.b: Remain separated, filtered, and limited to approved uses
options.c: Hold untreated gray water in the tank for at least 72 hours
options.d: Include kitchen-sink waste and toilet discharge in the same tank

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Where permitted, gray-water systems must stay physically separated from potable piping, meet filtration/disinfection and storage limits, and serve only approved uses such as subsurface irrigation. Kitchen waste and soil waste are blackwater, not gray water.

distractorExplanations.a: A single check valve is not backflow protection; gray water must not interconnect with potable piping.
distractorExplanations.c: Codes typically cap untreated storage (often about 24 hours) to limit odor and bacterial growth.
distractorExplanations.d: Toilet discharge is blackwater; many codes also exclude kitchen sinks from gray-water collection.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: An apprentice cannot tell how a waste stack turns from a floor plan alone. What does an isometric plumbing drawing show that a plan view does not?

options.a: A scaled plan view of piping as seen from directly above
options.b: A single-wall elevation of fixture heights on one face
options.c: A 3D-style view of pipe runs used to read the routing
options.d: A building cross-section showing structural member loads

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Isometric plumbing drawings show piping in a 3D-style view, typically with 30-degree offsets, so vertical stacks and horizontal runs can be read on one sheet. Plan and elevation views are 2D; structural sections are not plumbing isometrics.

distractorExplanations.a: A plan is a top-down 2D view; an isometric is drawn to show three-dimensional routing.
distractorExplanations.b: Elevations show one wall face; they do not replace a system-wide isometric.
distractorExplanations.d: Structural sections show building loads; they are not used to lay out plumbing isometrics.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: During a restaurant remodel, both a plumbing inspector and a health inspector walk the kitchen. What may the health department specifically regulate?

options.a: Branch circuit wiring for water heaters, pumps, and disposers
options.b: Structural notching and boring limits at plumbing holes
options.c: The utility's rate schedule for municipal water service
options.d: Plumbing sanitation in food sites and public health facilities

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Health departments commonly overlay extra sanitary rules on food-service and public-health plumbing—indirect wastes, mop sinks, grease control, and hand-wash fixtures. Electrical, structural, and utility-rate issues belong to other agencies.

distractorExplanations.a: Electrical inspectors enforce wiring to equipment; health departments do not adopt the electrical code.
distractorExplanations.b: Notching and boring limits are building-code structural rules, not health-department plumbing.
distractorExplanations.c: Water rates are a utility or commission matter, not a health-department plumbing regulation.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A reduced-pressure principle assembly on a boiler fill is specified as ASSE 1013. What do ASSE standards typically cover?

options.a: Backflow preventers and related plumbing-device performance
options.b: Fitting dimensions in the ASME B16 product-standards series
options.c: The model plumbing code text adopted by states and cities
options.d: Fire-sprinkler installation rules under NFPA 13 standards

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: ASSE (now IAPMO/ASSE) writes performance standards for plumbing devices—backflow preventers, mixing valves, and similar products. Model codes come from ICC or IAPMO; B16 is ASME; sprinkler installation is NFPA 13.

distractorExplanations.b: ASME B16 covers fitting dimensions; it is not an ASSE plumbing-device performance standard.
distractorExplanations.c: IPC and UPC are model codes; ASSE publishes device standards, not the adopted code text.
distractorExplanations.d: NFPA 13 governs sprinkler installation; ASSE 1013 is a backflow-preventer performance standard.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: The adopted IPC table shows a 12-inch bury, but the city ordinance requires water service 42 inches deep. What may local code amendments legally do?

options.a: Apply to a single permit instead of the whole jurisdiction
options.b: Modify the model code for local climate or soil conditions
options.c: Take effect from an inspector's verbal preference alone
options.d: Replace the adopted code with manufacturer instructions

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Governing bodies adopt the model code by ordinance and may amend it for local conditions such as frost depth, seismic rules, or water quality. Amendments apply jurisdiction-wide; a verbal inspector preference or a one-job deal is not an amendment.

distractorExplanations.a: A one-job change is a variance or modification, not a code amendment.
distractorExplanations.c: Amendments must be formally adopted; an inspector's preference is not code.
distractorExplanations.d: Manufacturer instructions apply through listings; they do not replace the adopted code.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A new DWV stack is plugged and ready for the inspector. What is the common model-code tightness test for drainage and vent piping?

options.a: A 5-foot water head or 3 psi air held 15 minutes with no loss
options.b: A 10-foot water head or 5 psi air held 5 minutes with no loss
options.c: A 10-foot water head or 5 psi air held 15 minutes with no loss
options.d: A 100 psi water or 50 psi air test held 15 minutes with no loss

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: IPC/UPC DWV testing commonly requires a 10-foot water column or a 5 psi air test held 15 minutes with no pressure or water-level loss. Water-supply tests use much higher pressures and must not be applied to DWV piping.

distractorExplanations.a: A 5-foot head or 3 psi air is below the usual 10-foot / 5 psi DWV test.
distractorExplanations.b: The pressure values match, but the hold time is 15 minutes, not 5.
distractorExplanations.d: Those pressures belong to water-distribution tests; they can damage DWV joints.

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.prompt: A helper wants to sit the journeyman exam after two weeks of carrying pipe. What does a typical journeyman plumber license require?

options.a: Completing a short online quiz with no documented field hours
options.b: Skipping apprenticeship, related instruction, and field hours
options.c: Showing a deed or lease in the licensing city or county
options.d: Completing documented experience and passing the trade exam

plumbing-journeyman-readiness-check-code.explanation: Most jurisdictions require documented apprenticeship or equivalent hours plus a trade exam before issuing a journeyman plumber license. A two-week helper stint, an online quiz, or property ownership does not meet those experience and testing requirements.

distractorExplanations.a: Licensing boards require documented hours and a proctored trade exam, not a short online quiz.
distractorExplanations.b: Apprenticeship or equivalent supervised experience is the usual path, not a waiver of all training.
distractorExplanations.c: Homeownership is unrelated to trade competence or licensing eligibility.
